components.claim_span: Chooses a valid strategy for comparing two unlike fractions — equivalent fractions, a benchmark such as one half, or a visual model

components.component: Carries the chosen strategy through to a comparison result
components.evidence: Items 1–3 require a written symbol ("write `<`, `>`, or `=`"), which can only be produced by carrying the chosen strategy through.

components.claim_span: shows the reasoning that supports the symbol

components.evidence: Part A: "Then show how you know", plus the header instruction "Show all work".

coverage.why: Each of the three moves the claim names — choosing among the named strategies, executing the chosen one, and showing reasoning tied to the symbol — is exercised by every item in Part A, and Part A asks for the choice rather than prescribing it.

conditions_support.conditions_reason: Supervision is declared "proctored_in_class" with resources limited to paper and pencil, and the teacher's novelty note says these particular numbers and problems are new to the students, so the comparison work on the page was produced in the room in a form the student could not have prepared.
conditions_support.conditions_supports: The teacher may conclude that each student, working alone with paper and pencil in 25 minutes, chose and carried out a comparison strategy and wrote the reasoning behind the symbol.

intended_inference.why: The conditions block states the teacher needs to conclude that each student individually can do what the claim names; purpose is summative and the work is individual.

materiality.why: Nothing the claim names goes unexercised, and the declared proctored, individual, novel-item conditions supply exactly the individual attribution the teacher's intended inference requires.

claims.supports: That each student individually chose a valid comparison strategy for unlike fractions, executed it, and showed the reasoning behind the comparison symbol, on number pairs new to them.

delegation.reason: Under proctored in-class administration with only paper and pencil and AI prohibited and enforced, there is no channel through which the comparison work could have been produced by anyone but the student.

conditions_echo: Grade 5 mathematics, end of Unit 4, 25 minutes, summative. Declared: proctored_in_class supervision, individual work, AI prohibited and enforced, resources limited to paper and pencil, item types practised but these particular numbers and problems new to students. Individual, independent attribution is required for every claim.
reviewer_notes: Attribution is strong for all five claims and is not the pressure point anywhere in this assessment: proctored, individual, paper-and-pencil administration on unfamiliar numbers meets the independent and novel conditions throughout, so the results license individual conclusions. Four of the five claims are carried in full, two of them with more items than the claim needs. The single limitation is one of coverage on G5C2a: the paper says "Answers in simplest form" but every computed result on it — 5/6, 7/12, 4 1/12, 1 7/12, 5/12, 3/4 — already arrives in lowest terms, so the simplifying move is never occasioned and a correct paper says nothing about whether the student can reduce. G5C2b, the parallel 'when the item requires it' claim, is by contrast genuinely required by items 6 and 7. This is a diagnosis of what the evidence licenses; no change to the assessment is proposed or implied.
